messages:
Maria: quick heads-up — after last night's kernel selector change (v2.14) we're seeing a p99 spike for non-streaming completions on the A100 pool. Streaming chat p99 looks stable. filing initial observations here so we don't duplicate work

Liam: can you paste the numbers and which workload? small text-complete requests or long-form?

Maria: smallish completions (avg seq_out ~ 32). perf snapshot: 
```
Before (v2.13): p50=18ms p95=70ms p99=140ms throughput=120req/s
After (v2.14):  p50=20ms p95=75ms p99=420ms throughput=118req/s
KV cache miss rate went from 2.1% -> 8.9% on the non-streaming path
```
Not massive throughput regression but tail is bad. suspect kernel fallback / handshake prefetch behavior for non-streaming path.

Anjali: interesting — streaming chat uses the streaming handshake which triggers early KV prefetch and tends to keep fast kernel affinity. non-streaming path does a single-shot route that sometimes picks the slow kernel for first chunk -> KV miss -> long tail. did we change kernel-prefetch heuristic in v2.14?

Kai: yes, v2.14 changed kernel chooser: it added "latency-robust" fallback that prefers the conservative kernel if batch_average_seq > 128 or if predicted_kv_miss_prob > 0.35. bug: predicted_kv_miss_prob model uses a feature that was zeroed for single-request microbatches (mb_size=1) after refactor. so many non-streaming small requests looked like "high miss" and got conservative kernel.

Maria: that explains why streaming (which uses client-side streaming microbatches and mb_size>1 in the pool) isn't affected. we need two things: short-term mitigation + a better heuristic.

Liam: short-term mitigation: bias kernel chooser to prefer fast kernel for non-streaming requests when seq_out < 64 and mb_size <= 2. can we roll that as a config flag?

Kai: yeah patch ready, small flip: `prefer_fast_for_small_nonstream=true`. quick canary please.

devops-bot: starting canary deploy of feature flag prefer_fast_for_small_nonstream=true to pool-a100-canary at 1705004400

BuildBot: canary deployed to pool-a100-canary (3hosts) — smoke ok.

Anjali: while the canary warms, longer-term idea: make kernel affinity use a two-stage signal: (1) handshake-prefetch indicator (boolean — did KV prefetch succeed during handshake) and (2) observed kv-miss-stamp within the request first N tokens. That avoids relying solely on ML prediction which broke here.

Maria: +1. proposal for heuristics doc:
- if streaming=true -> keep streaming fast-path (mb hysteresis as today)
- else if seq_out < 64 and mb_size <= 2 -> prefer fast kernel (low-latency path)
- else if handshake_prefetch==true -> prefer fast kernel
- else if observed_kv_miss_rate_first5 > 0.4 -> switch to conservative kernel for remainder of request
- emit metric `kernel_affinity_reason` (tags: fast, conservative, prefetched, predicted_high_miss)

Liam: also add a microbatching tweak: for non-streaming completions, allow short time-window coalescing (3-5ms) to form mb_size 2-4 when QPS high. That reduces number of mb_size=1 cases that hit the ML predictor hole. impacts latency slightly but reduces p99 a lot in our sim.

Kai: ran offline sim with client trace (100k reqs): adding 4ms coalesce + prefer_fast_for_small_nonstream cut p99 from 420ms -> 90ms, p95 75->72, throughput -1.5%. numbers: 
```
Sim result (trace-2026-03): p50=21ms p95=72ms p99=90ms throughput=116req/s
```
Logs show KV miss rate back to ~2.6%.

Maria: can we ship the flag cluster-wide after canary? and start emitting the new `kernel_affinity_reason` tag so SRE and product can monitor client-visible SLO impact?

devops-bot: canary healthy. rolling feature flag to pool-a100 (stage) at 1705004522

BuildBot: roll to stage completed.

Anjali: I'll open a short RFC for the two-stage signal and add a small telemetry dashboard: time-series for `kernel_affinity_reason`, `kv_miss_rate_first5`, `p99_nonstream` per model and per pool. also include a breakdown by client-traffic (PLG vs enterprise).

Maria: thx. action items: 1) Kai: promote flag to prod and add unit tests for predictor zeroing (ETA today EOD). 2) Anjali: RFC + dashboard (ETA EOD tomorrow). 3) Liam: run full QPS replay on prod pool next 24h and post results.

Kai: starting prod flip now (preferred-fast for small nonstream). ETA ~10m. will post logs.

Maria: thanks everyone. follow-up in #eng-runtime if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
